title: Binary Search
statement: Given a **sorted** array of distinct integers `nums` and a `target`, return the index of `target`, or −1 if it is not in the array. The algorithm must run in O(log n) time.
idea: Checking every element is O(n), but that ignores the fact that the array is sorted.
Look at the **middle** element. If it is too small, the target cannot be in the left half at all; if it is too big, it cannot be in the right half.
Either way, half of the remaining elements are discarded with one comparison. Repeating that leaves at most log₂ n steps.

complexity.timeWhy: Every comparison halves the range that is left.

steps.text: Our example: **`nums = [1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15,17], target = 11`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
`left` and `right` mark the part of the array where the target could still be. At first that is everything.
Look at the middle of that part: index 4, which holds **9**.
9 is **smaller** than 11. The array is sorted, so the target cannot be at index 4 or anywhere left of it. Discard that half: `left` = 5.
Look at the middle of that part: index 6, which holds **13**.
13 is **bigger** than 11, so the target cannot be at index 6 or anywhere right of it. Discard that half: `right` = 5.
Look at the middle of that part: index 5, which holds **11**.
11 is the target. Found at index **5**.
Done — the answer is **`5`**. nums[5] is 11.
